text: Azure SQL's point-in-time restore only protects data inside Azure, so a nightly step exports the storefront database to a portable dot bacpac file in a Blob Storage container -- a backup that can actually live outside Azure.
A separate scheduled workflow runs every night at 07:00 UTC, downloads that latest export from Blob Storage, and uploads it into the driftwood-app-backups S3 bucket from Lesson 6.

The job authenticates to Azure with the same OIDC pattern from Lesson 5, and to AWS the same way: GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged for short-lived credentials scoped to exactly the replication role Lesson 6 already wrote the IAM policy for.
No AWS access key or secret key is ever stored in GitHub Secrets on either side of this job -- both clouds trust a short-lived token, not a standing credential.
Running aws s3 ls against the bucket after a scheduled run shows a new dated prefix, confirming the chain works end to end. Lesson 8 puts all of it together for the first real production deploy.
